vocab.term: What do you do for a living?
vocab.example: So, what do you do for a living?
I work as a sales manager.
In my free time, I go running by the Nile.
I'm really into photography. / I'm really into cooking.
What kind of music do you like?
“I design apps for hospitals.” “That sounds interesting.”
How long have you lived in Cairo?

options.label: Photography. I take photos of old buildings.

items.prompt: What do you do for a living?
How long have you lived here?
What kind of music do you like?
What do you do in your free time?
That sounds interesting. Do you like your job?

tasks.title: Write two follow-up questions
tasks.instructions: Read each sentence. Write two questions to keep the conversation going. Use the expressions from the lesson.
models: Oh, really? Which team do you support? How long have you played?
What kind of hospital do you work in? Do you enjoy it?

items.prompt: “In my free time, I bake cakes.”

tasks.title: Find and fix the mistake
tasks.instructions: Each sentence has one mistake. Write the correct sentence.

answer: How long have you lived here?

items.prompt: I work like a doctor in a big hospital.
answer: I work as a doctor in a big hospital.

items.prompt: What kind music do you like?
answer: What kind of music do you like?

items.prompt: I'm really into to play tennis.
What do you do for living?
answer: What do you do for a living?

tasks.title: Write a message
tasks.instructions: Last night you met someone new at a party. Write them a WhatsApp message (50–70 words). Use the frame.

parts.label: 1 · Say hello
parts.hint: Hi Sara! It was really nice to meet you last night.

parts.label: 2 · Remember something they said
parts.hint: You said you're really into … That sounds …

parts.label: 3 · Ask a question
parts.hint: How long have you …? / What kind of …?

parts.label: 5 · Suggest meeting again
parts.hint: Would you like to … next week?

tasks.title: Record yourself
tasks.instructions: Record a 1-minute voice note. Listen, then record a better version.
steps: Talk about your job, your free time and one thing you're really into.
End with a question for the listener: “How about you? What are you into?”
Listen. Did you use at least 4 expressions from the lesson?
Record it again. Speak a little slower and add one more detail.
Send your best version to your trainer.
tasks.reflection: Which expressions did you use? What will you improve?

tasks.title: Real-life mission
tasks.instructions: Try the three-question rule in a real conversation this week.
steps: Choose a person: a colleague, a friend, or someone in an online group.
Ask one question, then two follow-up questions about the same topic.
Write down one interesting thing you learned about them.
Tell your trainer about it in your next session.
tasks.reflection: Who did you talk to, and what interesting thing did you learn about them?
